subject: Lumatech collection rails: SGD/BRL inflows, intermediary bank fee responsibility & VAT handling
messages:
From: Carlos Mendez <treasury@lumatech.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Payment rails question for INV-2027-08921 (SGD / BRL)

Hi Stephanie,

Quick question on the invoice we received (INV-2027-08921). We have two legal entities paying: Lumatech APAC (will pay in SGD) and Lumatech Brazil (BRL). Our treasury ops team flagged that when we route SGD into your Singapore nostro, intermediary banks sometimes debit a flat fee that ends up deducted after you invoice (we assume SHA charges). For BRL payments our local bank wants to use a correspondent bank in the US which also triggers intermediary fees and currency conversion windows.

Can you confirm:
- Which beneficiary account and account reference we should use for SGD and BRL so the funds net to Redwood without a mismatch to the invoice?
- Do you require the customer to set charges to OUR (customer pays all intermediaries) or is SHA acceptable? If SHA, who should absorb the residual intermediary debits?
- Any VAT/reverse-charge requirements we should include on our remittance (we're in APAC and LATAM for these invoices)?

I've attached the invoice and our proposed wire template. Happy to schedule a short call if easier.

Thanks,
Carlos
Treasury Manager
Lumatech Inc.
attachments: INV-2027-08921.pdf, wire_template_lumatech.xlsx

Hi Carlos — thanks for the clear note and attachments. Quick answers up front, then some nitty-gritty:

Short summary
- SGD: please route to our Redwood Singapore USD/SGD collection account (details below) and use the invoice number in beneficiary reference. Set charges=SHA only if you confirm intermediary banks will not deduct after credit (we prefer OUR where possible).
- BRL: because BRL flows typically transit a USD correspondent, please use YOUR bank's cover instruction with OUR for the USD leg so amounts match the invoice; otherwise we frequently see a small shortfall.
- VAT: for APAC/SGD no VAT on our SaaS invoice (zero-rated export in most APAC locales), for BRL please include any local tax ID on remittance for reconciliation — we'll accept gross or net but need trace code if intermediaries debit.

Proposed beneficiary templates (for your bank):
- SGD inflow (Redwood SG nostros):
  Account name: Redwood Inference Pte Ltd
  Account number: 312-045-998
  Bank: DBS Bank Ltd
  SWIFT: DBSSSGSG
  Beneficiary reference: INV-2027-08921 / Lumatech APAC
  Charges: OUR preferred; SHA acceptable if your bank confirms no after-debit.

- BRL inflow (cover via USD correspondent recommended):
  Beneficiary (final): Redwood Inference Inc. (US)
  Beneficiary account (USD): 00123456789
  Bank: First US Correspondent Bank
  SWIFT: FUSCUS33
  Cover instruction: Please instruct your BRL bank to convert to USD and send as "OUR" on the USD cover to avoid deductions, or provide pre-funded USD cover.

Cc'ing Marissa from Payments Ops to confirm there are no ledger-side constraints. If you prefer, we can take the SGD via our DBS SGD nostro and BRL via a USD cover (we will post to the invoice as the USD equivalent at payment date).

Let me know if you want a brief call and what times work.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the heads up — operational guidance below.

Policy / ops notes (Marissa, Payments Ops)
- SGD (DBS SG nostros): we can accept SHA for trusted enterprise customers if the customer confirms their bank does not perform after-market debits. If an intermediary debit posts and reduces the received amount, we will ticket for recovery but reconciliation can take 7–10 business days. For DEAL-4882 (enterprise), recommend asking Lumatech to set charges=OUR for SGD where possible.
- BRL flows: BECAUSE BRL tends to convert locally and route via a USD correspondent, insist on OUR on the USD cover leg. If customer cannot send OUR, request they include expected intermediary fee amount on remittance so we can reconcile differences quickly.
- Shortfall tolerance: Redwood Finance will not auto-write off shortfalls > USD 10. For amounts <= USD 10 we can absorb once per quarter per account as a courtesy; anything above must be recovered.
- VAT: Redwood classifies the invoice as export SaaS (no VAT for SG remits). For BRL, if Lumatech requires withholding tax treatment locally, we need a certificate of tax withholding and/or local tax ID (CNPJ) on the remittance.

Suggested reply to Lumatech: include the two beneficiary templates, ask them to confirm 'OUR' where possible for BRL, and request a screenshot of the outgoing wire instruction if they choose SHA so we can pre-check the reference field. Also attach the canonical wire template (I updated it) — see wire_template_lumatech.xlsx.

Marissa
Payments Operations Manager
Redwood Inference

Carlos / team — thanks for the patience. Confirming Redwood's recommended instructions and next steps so your ops can send payment without reconciliation friction: 

1) SGD payment (Lumatech APAC)\- Use the Redwood Singapore SGD nostro (DBS). Beneficiary reference must exactly include "INV-2027-08921" and "Lumatech APAC".
- Charges: OUR preferred. If your bank uses SHA please send a screenshot of the outgoing instruction in advance so Redwood Payments can pre-authorize; note we may still see an intermediary debit after credit.

2) BRL payment (Lumatech Brazil)\- Because BRL will route via a USD correspondent in many cases, instruct your bank to push a USD cover with charges=OUR on the USD leg, or pre-fund the USD cover. This prevents the common sub-USD shortfalls and speeds reconciliation. If you cannot send OUR, include the Estimated intermediary fee in the remittance field (e.g., "expected intermediary fee USD X") so we can match.

3) VAT / tax pieces\- For SGD: Redwood considers this export of services — no Singapore GST applied on our invoice; include your APAC tax ID in remittance for your records.
- For BRL: if Brazil imposes withholding on your side, please provide the withholding tax certificate and the CNPJ on remittance so Redwood Finance can apply the correct credit.

4) Tolerances and recovery\- Redwood will not absorb shortfalls > USD 10. For <= USD 10 we can absorb once per quarter as a courtesy for enterprise customers; otherwise we'll open recovery.

Attachments: updated wire_template_lumatech.xlsx (canonical fields filled) and the invoice. Please confirm which payment method you'll use (SGD via DBS nostro + BRL via USD cover, or alternative) and send the outgoing instruction screenshot if you elect SHA charges. If it's helpful, happy to jump on a 20-minute call with treasury ops — propose Fri 24 Sep 10:00 SGT / 23 Sep 22:00 EDT.

Best regards,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
